subject.title: Feature Request: Batch API support for background tasks

question: Should OpenClaw adopt a generic delayed-agent-turn contract, and which background surface should be the first supported caller?
rationale: The choice defines a public Plugin SDK lifecycle, persistent state ownership, provider fallback and billing semantics, and user-visible configuration across several execution surfaces; source inspection cannot determine the intended product boundary.

options.title: Generic contract, cron first
options.body: Design an additive provider lifecycle and initially expose it only for isolated cron agentTurn jobs before expanding to other background callers.

options.title: All background surfaces together
options.body: Design cron, heartbeat, sessions_send, and sessions_spawn opt-ins as one larger coordinated feature with shared lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Defer Batch API support
options.body: Keep immediate streaming turns as the only supported agent execution mode and leave discounted batch workloads outside OpenClaw for now.

recommendation.title: Generic contract, cron first
recommendation.body: Design an additive provider lifecycle and initially expose it only for isolated cron agentTurn jobs before expanding to other background callers.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history and issue discussion most strongly connect this person to both the provider-runtime and cron decision surfaces.
